title: Fourth-moment tail bound for $B$-reasonable variables
statement: Let $X\in L^4$ on a probability space, let $B\ge1$, and suppose $\E X^4\le B(\E X^2)^2$, $X^4$ is integrable, and $\E X^2>0$. For every $t>0$, $\Pr[X^4\ge t^4(\E X^2)^2]\le B/t^4$.
hypotheses_covered: second moment E[X^2] is strictly positive
replaced:
If $X$ is $B$-reasonable and not equivalent to $0$ (its second moment is positive), then for
every $t > 0$,
\[
\Pr\bigl[\,|X| \ge t\,\norm{X}_2\,\bigr] \le \frac{B}{t^4}.
\]
